speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help me diagnose your condition, please describe exactly when the pain started, how sharp or squeezing it feels, and if you have experienced any shortness of breath or sweating.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (spontaneous esophageal rupture).

The history of forceful retching after heavy alcohol consumption followed by sudden chest pain and choking is a classic presentation for esophageal rupture. I need to confirm your current vital signs, specifically looking for signs of sepsis or shock like low blood pressure or a high fever, and I need to see a Chest X-ray to look for a mediastinal air-fluid level or pleural effusion. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray; REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
